text.tspan: # MOAR players, MOAR bottles, MOAR memes — the rendezvous, ramped up
`Rendezvous.lean` told the whole orientability story on the **four**-cycle with
the **two**-bottle swap: orientable iff an even number of the four edges flip.
This file *ramps it up*. It keeps the same moral — "orientability is decided by
the parity of the number of swaps" — but proves it in maximal generality:
* **MOAR players.** The exchange cycle has `Fin n` players for *any* `n`, not
just four. Walking the cycle `0 → 1 → ⋯ → n-1 → 0` and composing the `n`
* **MOAR bottles.** The fibre being permuted is an *arbitrary* finite type `B`
of bottles with two distinguished ones `a ≠ b`, not just the ordered pair of
* **MOAR structure.** The ℤ/2 orientation class is realized honestly as the
**permutation sign** of the holonomy: each swap-edge contributes a genuine
transposition `Equiv.swap a b`, whose sign is `-1`, so the total holonomy has
sign `(-1)^(number of swap-edges)`. Non-orientability is then *literally* an
* **The model.** `EdgeSwaps n = Fin n → Bool` records, for each of the `n`
peer-transitions of the cycle, whether a genuine swap is inserted.
`edgePerm a b e i` is the transition permutation on edge `i`
(`Equiv.swap a b` on flipped edges, `1` otherwise), and `holonomy a b e` is the
ordered product of all `n` transition maps around the cycle.

- `orientationClass_eq_swapCount` — the ℤ/2 orientation class is the swap-count
* **Orientable ⇔ even, Klein ⇔ odd — for any n, any bottles.**
- `orientable_iff_even` — the holonomy is an *even* permutation (sign `1`) iff

* **The old four-cycle two-bottle story is the special case.** With more players
and more bottles the conclusion is unchanged: `single_edge_nonorientable`
(one swap anywhere is non-orientable), `no_edge_orientable` (no swaps is
`n` is even), and the checkable spec `isKleinShaped_iff_odd`.
/-- A rendezvous edge-assignment on the `n`-cycle of players: for each of the `n`
peer-transitions `i → i+1`, whether a genuine swap is inserted (`true`) or the
abbrev EdgeSwaps (n : ℕ) : Type := Fin n → Bool
/-- The number of peer-transitions that carry a genuine swap. -/
(Finset.univ.filter (fun i : Fin n => e i = true)).card
/-- The transition permutation on edge `i`: the transposition `Equiv.swap a b`
of the two distinguished bottles where a swap is inserted, the identity
def edgePerm (a b : B) (e : EdgeSwaps n) : Fin n → Equiv.Perm B :=
fun i => if e i then Equiv.swap a b else 1
/-- The holonomy of the rendezvous: the ordered product of all `n` transition
maps around the exchange cycle `0 → 1 → ⋯ → n-1 → 0`. -/
def holonomy (a b : B) (e : EdgeSwaps n) : Equiv.Perm B :=
(List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => edgePerm a b e i)).prod
/-- The ℤ/2 orientation class: the total twist accumulated around the cycle. -/
∑ i : Fin n, (if e i then (1 : ZMod 2) else 0)
/-- The sign of a single transition map: `-1` on a swap-edge, `1` otherwise. -/
theorem sign_edgePerm (a b : B) (hab : a ≠ b) (e : EdgeSwaps n) (i : Fin n) :
Equiv.Perm.sign (edgePerm a b e i) = if e i then -1 else 1 := by
**The sign of the holonomy is `-1` to the swap-count.** Each swap-edge
inserts a transposition with sign `-1`; multiplicativity of the sign turns the
holonomy's sign into `(-1)^(number of swap-edges)`. This is the ramped-up
statement that the orientation class *is* the permutation sign.
theorem sign_holonomy (a b : B) (hab : a ≠ b) (e : EdgeSwaps n) :
Equiv.Perm.sign (holonomy a b e) = (-1) ^ (swapCount e) := by
-- The sign of a product of permutations is the product of their signs.
have h_sign_prod : ∀ (l : List (Equiv.Perm B)), sign (List.prod l) = List.prod (List.map sign l) := by
rw [ Finset.prod_congr rfl fun i _ => sign_edgePerm a b hab e i, Finset.prod_ite ] ; simp +decide [ swapCount ]
**The orientation class is the swap-count mod 2** — for any number of
/-- The rendezvous is **orientable** when its holonomy is an even permutation. -/
def Orientable (a b : B) (e : EdgeSwaps n) : Prop :=
**Orientable ⇔ an even number of edges swap** — for any players, any
theorem orientable_iff_even (a b : B) (hab : a ≠ b) (e : EdgeSwaps n) :
Orientable a b e ↔ Even (swapCount e) := by
rw [ Moar.sign_holonomy a b hab e ];
/-- **Non-orientable ⇔ an odd number of edges swap.** The holonomy is a genuine
*odd* permutation exactly when the swap-count is odd. -/
theorem nonorientable_iff_odd (a b : B) (hab : a ≠ b) (e : EdgeSwaps n) :
¬ Orientable a b e ↔ Odd (swapCount e) := by
rw [orientable_iff_even a b hab e, Nat.not_even_iff_odd]
/-- The all-straight rendezvous: no transition flips. -/
def noEdge (n : ℕ) : EdgeSwaps n := fun _ => false
/-- The all-swap rendezvous: every transition flips. -/
def allEdge (n : ℕ) : EdgeSwaps n := fun _ => true
/-- The rendezvous with a swap on exactly one peer-relation `j`. -/
def singleEdge (j : Fin n) : EdgeSwaps n := fun i => decide (i = j)
theorem swapCount_singleEdge (j : Fin n) : swapCount (singleEdge j) = 1 := by
theorem swapCount_allEdge : swapCount (allEdge n) = n := by
/-- **No swaps is orientable** — for any players, any bottles. -/
theorem no_edge_orientable (a b : B) (hab : a ≠ b) :
/-- **A swap on any single peer-relation is non-orientable** — whichever edge it
is, and however many players and bottles there are. One transposition is an odd
theorem single_edge_nonorientable (a b : B) (hab : a ≠ b) (j : Fin n) :
/-- **Everyone swapping is orientable iff the number of players is even.** With
`n` players all flipping, the holonomy is `(-1)^n`, so it is an even permutation
exactly when `n` is even — the natural generalization of "four swaps is a
theorem all_edge_orientable_iff (a b : B) (hab : a ≠ b) :
Orientable a b (allEdge n) ↔ Even n := by
/-! ## The design constraint as a checkable spec -/
/-- A rendezvous protocol is **Klein-shaped by construction** when its holonomy
def IsKleinShaped (a b : B) (e : EdgeSwaps n) : Prop :=
/-- **The spec, ramped up.** For any number of players and any bottles, a
rendezvous is Klein-shaped iff the swap appears on an *odd* number of the cycle's
peer-relations — a condition checkable directly against `swapCount`. -/
theorem isKleinShaped_iff_odd (a b : B) (hab : a ≠ b) (e : EdgeSwaps n) :
IsKleinShaped a b e ↔ Odd (swapCount e) :=
/-! ## The artifact: rendering the ramped-up rendezvous as an animated SVG
Everything below is ordinary, terminating `IO`/`String` code. It draws a whole
ring of players passing a whole shelf of bottles, marks which peer-transitions
insert a genuine swap, reads off the parity, and scrolls the full source of this
file — the ramp-up itself — sealed inside. "MOAR players, MOAR bottles, MOAR
/-- Escape the five XML-significant characters so arbitrary source text is safe
/-- A tiny deterministic linear-congruential generator, so the starfield is
/-- Round a `Float` to the nearest integer. -/
/-- Half of Ludolph's number, plenty accurate for layout. -/
/-- Number of players around the ramped-up ring. -/
/-- Which of the `nPlayers` peer-transitions insert a genuine swap. This is a
concrete `EdgeSwaps nPlayers` given as a `Bool` list; it has an *odd* number of
swaps, so the holonomy is a genuine odd permutation — non-orientable (Klein). -/
[true, false, false, true, false, true, false, false, true, false, false, true]
/-- Position of player `i` on the ring of radius `R` about `(cx, cy)`. -/
def nodePos (i : Nat) (cx cy R : Float) : Int × Int :=
let theta := 2.0 * piF * (Float.ofNat i) / (Float.ofNat nPlayers) - piF / 2.0
(iround (cx + R * Float.cos theta), iround (cy + R * Float.sin theta))
(List.range nPlayers).map (fun i => nodePos i ringCx ringCy ringR)
def starfield (n : Nat) : String := Id.run do
s!"<circle cx=\"{x}\" cy=\"{y}\" r=\"{r}\" fill=\"#cfe3ff\" opacity=\"0\">\
/-- Draw the ring edges: teal dashes for straight transitions, a pink crossing
twist for swap transitions. Swap edges also carry two tokens that cross over
(the exchange), straight edges a single token passed along. -/
-- pink swap edge, drawn as an X-crossing, with two tokens exchanging
/-- Draw the players (bottle glyphs) around the ring, each labelled `Pi`. -/
/-- Scattered doge-style "MOAR" memes, because more memes. -/
"<text x=\"400\" y=\"120\" class=\"meme meme1\">wow. odd ⇒ Klein</text>"
/-- Split the source into `<tspan>` lines for the sealed scrolling column. -/
def sourceTspans (src : String) : String := Id.run do
out := out ++ s!"<tspan x=\"382\" dy=\"11\">{xmlEscape l}</tspan>"
/-- CSS for the animation (kept as a plain string literal so `{ }` are literal). -/
.player { font-family:'DejaVu Sans Mono',monospace; font-size:12px; fill:#eaf2ff; font-weight:700; }
.glob { font-family:'DejaVu Sans Mono',monospace; font-size:20px; fill:#ff9bcf; font-weight:700; }
.meme { font-family:'Comic Sans MS','DejaVu Sans',sans-serif; font-size:20px; font-weight:700; }
/-- Assemble the whole self-contained animated SVG. -/
let parity := if swapK % 2 == 0 then "+1" else "-1"
let verdict := if swapK % 2 == 0 then "ORIENTABLE (torus)" else "NON-ORIENTABLE (Klein)"
s!"a ring of {nPlayers} players swapping bottles — orientability is the parity of the swaps, checked in Lean 4</text>\n"
s!"<text x=\"450\" y=\"476\" text-anchor=\"middle\" class=\"globsub\">{swapK} swaps ⇒ {verdict}</text>\n"
header ++ defs ++ background ++ ringEdges ++ ringNodes ++ core ++
/-- Read this file's own source so it can be sealed inside the artifact. -/
return "-- (source not located at runtime; the theorems still stand) --"
/-- The side effect: render the ramped-up rendezvous as an animated SVG. -/
